artifact.category_tag: semiclassical analysis of semitoric integrable systems
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a connected symplectic 4-manifold and let $(F_1,F_2):M\to\mathbb{R}^2$ be a semitoric integrable system, meaning that $F_1,F_2$ Poisson-commute, the flow of $F_1$ generates an effective $S^1$-action with proper momentum map, and all singularities of $F=(F_1,F_2)$ are non-degenerate with no hyperbolic blocks. Assume $F$ has a focus-focus singular fiber. Consider a semiclassical quantization of $F$: a pair $(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))$ of commuting self-adjoint semiclassical (pseudodifferential or Berezin–Toeplitz) operators depending on a small parameter $\hbar\in(0,\hbar_0]$, with respective principal symbols $F_1,F_2$. Near the focus-focus critical value, the joint spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ admits a description by singular Bohr–Sommerfeld quantization rules expressible as a formal power series in $\hbar$ (with $\log\hbar$ terms) whose coefficients are smooth functions on a punctured neighborhood of the critical value; call this series the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld series associated to the focus-focus point.
 
Question: Is the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series in $\hbar$ a spectral invariant? Equivalently, is it determined—term by term and uniquely—by the joint semiclassical spectrum $\mathrm{JointSpec}(P_1(\hbar),P_2(\hbar))$ as $\hbar\to 0^+$, in the sense that any two such quantizations with the same joint spectrum (modulo $O(\hbar^\infty)$) produce the same singular Bohr–Sommerfeld series?
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work on the inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems (notably Le Floch–Pelayo, arXiv:2104.06704) recovers all symplectic invariants of a semitoric system from the semiclassical joint spectrum and shows semitoric systems are spectrally determined algorithmically; related works confirm that the Taylor-series invariant at focus-focus points can be read off the spectrum. This effectively answers the underlying inverse-spectral claim affirmatively in the semitoric case, but the precise statement that the singular Bohr–Sommerfeld formal power series itself is a spectral invariant (and its extensions beyond semitoric and to higher dimensions) has not been settled in full generality.

status_evidence.title: The inverse spectral problem for quantum semitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: explicit formulas for recovering, from the semiclassical asymptotics of the joint spectrum, all symplectic invariants of the underlying classical semitoric system... semitoric systems are completely spectrally determined in an algorithmic way
status_evidence.claim: The inverse spectral problem for semitoric systems has been resolved: symplectic invariants are recovered from the joint spectrum.

status_evidence.title: Singular Bohr-Sommerfeld rules for 2D integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: systems with focus-focus singularities have a universal behavior described by singular quantization conditions of Bohr-Sommerfeld type
status_evidence.claim: The singular Bohr–Sommerfeld rules give a precise description of the joint spectrum near focus-focus singularities.
